text:
Dallas won 5-0, and the scoreboard barely captures how one-sided it was. The Stars out-attempted San Jose 66 to 34 and piled up 4.76 expected goals against the Sharks' 1.57, which works out to a 92 percent chance of winning if every shot were replayed. Even with the power play removed, the gap held at 3.66 to 1.03. Dallas went 0 for 3 with the man advantage and still never needed it.

The game turned in the second period, when Dallas generated 2.01 expected goals and scored three times in 13 minutes. Joel Kiviranta opened it at 3:17 on a snap shot, a 63 percent chance and the best look of the night. Jamie Benn made it 3-0 at 6:19, and Jason Robertson added a wrist shot at 16:30 that made it 4-0. The first goal had come late in the opening period, when Miro Heiskanen beat Yaroslav Askarov on a backhand that carried only a 3 percent chance of going in. It was a small gift that changed the tone, and Dallas had already out-chanced San Jose 1.74 to 0.22 by then.

Askarov was not the main problem. He allowed 5 goals on 4.76 expected, so he was roughly what the chances predicted, just buried under volume. At the other end, Jake Oettinger faced 13 shots for the shutout and stopped everything, 1.57 expected goals worth of danger. Mikko Rantanen sealed it in the third at 15:22. Benn took first star with a goal and an assist, and the Stars never let San Jose settle.
